brief.scope: Independent acceptance design for authorized discovery contract step 1, parallel to Grok drafting. Read owner requirements and supplied MCP-fit review; inspect only necessary existing contracts. Do not read Grok's in-progress draft and do not repeat the whole-lane audit. Return <=1000-word acceptance matrix and high-value counterexamples for dev machinery and prod Symfony work: expected owner/tool answers, bounded startup/detail, zero/one/multiple/unreadable/stale/cross-profile handoffs, provenance/authority, missing metadata, source races, profile/harness independence, compatibility/CLI-MCP parity, malicious record text and no-write/no-network/no-arbitrary-command boundaries. Separate contract requirements from tests deferred to step 2. This is independent test-design input, not executable tests or an approval of Grok's plan (GPT-6 will review that). No edits, code, active settings/state or live host changes. Cite owning contract for each group; explicit unknowns. Inline artifact is sufficient.

artifacts.acceptance_matrix:
Contract requirements for step 1:

| Group | Required acceptance |
|---|---|
| Ownership and answers | A dev query for dispatch identifies `ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md` and the existing dispatch lever; a prod query identifies the intended Symfony package/service and Console/MCP projections, but reports implementation, installation, activation and live probe separately. It must not promote the home-map report into authority or invent a Symfony service. Owners: `AGENTS.md` Standing rulings; `ops/README.md`; `ops/conductor/README.md`; `docs/mapping.md`.
| Profiles and sources | Configuration is versioned and closed, with exactly `dev` and `prod` initially. Profiles select work context and authoritative sources; harness is an independent input. `codex prod` remains prod and `grok dev` remains dev. Requests accept logical concepts/IDs, never paths, argv or source overrides. Owners: owner brief, Owner requirements; `ops/lane.conf`; `ops/conductor/lane-mcp-lever.md` Configuration.
| Startup and detail | One startup query returns schema/version, selected profile, compact owner/tool cards, source revisions, action availability and handoff summary within 16,384 canonical bytes. Record text is excluded. Targeted detail is ID-and-revision addressed, at most 16,384 bytes per response; text pages retain the existing 8,192-byte bound and revision-bound continuation. Owners: owner brief, bounded startup requirement; `lane-mcp-lever.md` Four tools; `lane-mcp-v2.md` Revision/Bounds.
| Handoff selection | Zero eligible candidates: `state=ok`, empty candidates, null selection. Exactly one fresh, readable, profile-relevant candidate: selected without a supplied filesystem path. Multiple eligible candidates: explicit ambiguity and null selection. Unreadable candidates remain visible as unavailable; stale and cross-profile candidates carry those states and are never auto-selected. Missing profile, captured ref, time or lineage metadata remains visible as incomplete and prevents automatic selection. Owners: `ops/conductor/handoff/README.md`; `docs/probes.md`; owner brief Fresh-session acceptance.
| Provenance, freshness and races | Every owner/tool/candidate value identifies logical source, owning contract, captured ref or byte revision, observation time and freshness result. Evidence never becomes authority. Enumeration and detail must form one declared snapshot; a changed source/ref yields conflict/Abort and no mixed payload. A continuation revision mismatch refuses and requires restart. Owners: `docs/verified-couplings.md` obligations 3–5; `docs/wire.md`; `lane-mcp-v2.md` Revision/Cursor.
| Compatibility and projections | Existing v1/v2 configs and queries remain byte-identical. New discovery is opt-in through a declared version. Stationary source bytes produce identical canonical domain payloads through CLI query, MCP tool and MCP resource. CLI Rejection/Abort and MCP error results preserve expected–found–needed; absence, ambiguity and unavailability remain domain readings. Owners: `lane-mcp-lever.md` Compatibility/MCP transport; `instrument-conventions.md`; `docs/wire.md`.
| Trust and effects | Record Markdown, JSON strings, URI-like text and command-looking text are escaped data and never instructions. `lane_read` spawns no subprocess. Retained-ref acquisition is a separate fixed adapter accepting only profile/logical source and returning typed projections; no request-supplied path or argv. Neither projection writes files, refs, databases or worktrees, follows unapproved symlinks, reads credentials/user directories, or uses network. Owners: `lane-mcp-lever.md` Existing capability and boundary; `onboard-lever.md` Thread; owner brief Source allowlisting.
artifacts.counterexamples: High-value counterexamples: (1) one readable candidate plus one unreadable candidate must not select the readable one; the unreadable record may be the relevant one. (2) A fresh file mtime with an obsolete captured ref is stale. (3) A branch containing `dev` cannot supply missing profile metadata. (4) Two equally relevant handoffs cannot be resolved by filename, filesystem order or newest-only guessing. (5) A candidate changing between enumeration and detail must conflict, not combine old metadata with new text. (6) A `prod` profile launched through Codex must not expose dev-only context merely because Codex defaults appear in lane configuration. (7) A registry row proves declaration, not installation, activation or successful probing. (8) Text containing shell commands, prompt injection, traversal paths, control bytes or MCP-looking JSON must be returned only as bounded escaped data. (9) FIFO/device/symlink-loop/oversized/malformed sources are unavailable, never empty. (10) Legacy v1/v2 payload drift caused by new fields fails compatibility.
artifacts.deferred_step_2: Deferred executable tests: independent producers should later build synthetic adapter fixtures for the full profile×harness matrix; zero/one/multiple/unreadable/stale/cross-profile and missing-metadata rows; source mutation and revision cursors; hostile text and special files; legacy golden payloads; CLI/tool/resource parity; and before/after hashes of refs, files and databases plus a denied-network/command spy. Symfony tests must use contract-verified adapter mocks and prove the shared service drives both Console and MCP projections. Live host activation and harness enforcement require separate protocol probes; they are not discovery tests.
artifacts.unknowns: The step-1 contract still must decide the canonical retained-ref namespace, fixed enumeration adapter, authoritative home for profile metadata, relevance ordering, freshness threshold, action-entrypoint metadata, new schema/config version, and Symfony package name. Current measurement at target: `packages/` contains only README, `composer.lock` has `symfony/console` 8.1.6 but no MCP package, and `vendor/` is absent; therefore prod implementation and activation are unavailable, not inferred.

envelope.note: Independent contract-test design only; no Grok draft or session store was read, no plan was approved, and no files, settings, state, refs, network resources or host configuration were changed.
